children: has eliminated 145 corporate positions, about 4% of its corporate workforce, marking its third round of layoffs in less than a year as the used-car retailer works to streamline operations amid a challenging market.
The latest cuts follow the elimination of about 350 jobs in October 2025 and another 230 positions in January.
The company said the latest reduction is aimed at supporting its strategic priorities and operating with a leaner corporate workforce

faces pressure from high vehicle prices and interest rates that have weighed on used-car demand. CEO Keith Barr, who took over in March, is focused on improving customer experience while cutting costs.
